svg.title: Payment Posting Architecture
svg.text: Payment Posting — callback to posted in the LMS
Challan returned immediately · everything after is async · status check only on retry
1 · Synchronous — the only part anyone waits for
Challan from sequence · INSERT row · COMMIT
The challan is the commitment. No LMS call is waited for.
The status check is the resume mechanism.
A first attempt cannot be a duplicate, so the call is skipped —
about 25% fewer LMS calls in the normal path. On retry it tells us
whether a post landed before the last attempt was cut off.
Drawn by every executor on every server.
Agree the ceiling in the LMS team's unit —
a 4× misreading is how a limit becomes an outage.
One permit per transaction, not per call.
IN_FLIGHT — an executor is working it
Technical failure retries. Business rejection does not.
5 · Two records, two purposes — do not merge them
FETCH FIRST :batch ROWS ONLY FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
A row left IN_FLIGHT by a server that died is reclaimed only after 60 seconds, beyond
the LMS's own 30-second timeout. Without that floor, a sweeper on one server reclaims
a row an executor on another is still posting, and both call the LMS.
Completion is always conditional: WHERE STATUS = 'IN_FLIGHT'. Zero rows = already done.
1 · Vendor retries the callback → UNIQUE (partner, idem key) returns the original challan
2 · Two executors claim one row → FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
3 · Sweeper reclaims a live row → IN_FLIGHT + 60-second floor
4 · Retry after an LMS timeout → status check on every retry
5 · Status check misses a just-landed post → unique client reference
6 · Kafka redelivery → conditional UPDATE; zero rows = already done, ack anyway
1 · Do FAILED callbacks post to the LMS, or stop at NOT_APPLICABLE? 2 · What counts as an amount mismatch — exact, or a tolerance?
3 · Is the LMS post API idempotent on a client reference? 4 · Is the agreed ceiling in transactions or API calls? 5 · Retention for LMS_API_LOG?
